settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: The application's own: the values its lists are made of, the views people saved, and who may do what.

lookups.intro: The closed sets of values a record can take. The code is what is stored; the label is what a reader sees, in their language.
lookups.label: Label

categories.nameRequired: A category needs an English name.

views.intro: The arrangements of the tickets list you saved under a name. Each one opens from the list's view picker.
views.name: Name
views.deleteBody: “{name}” is no longer offered by the tickets list. The tickets themselves do not change.
views.emptyBody: Arrange the tickets list — a filter, a sort — and save it under a name from its view picker.

users.intro: The accounts that can sign in, and the roles each holds. A role given or taken here applies from that account's next sign-in.
users.name: Name

permissions.intro: What each role may do: the table the application's guards read.
permissions.introEdit: What each role may do: the table the application's guards read. A change applies at once, and the server checks every action again.

account.read: The account page: who is signed in, their role, their preferences.

billing.read: The billing figures on the account page.
billing.write: Closing the month. The server checks it again, whatever the page shows.

tickets.billing: The Billing tab of an intervention.

settings.permissions: This screen and Users: changing what a role may do, and who holds which role.
